notes: Decomposes the two highest-impact index-calculus frontier heuristics into finite, separately attackable yield and rank obligations. No new measurement or asymptotic claim is made.

sources.title: Yield and rank frontier decomposition
sources.notes: Scope and dependency audit of fixed-population decomposition yield, solver visibility, relation support and terminal rank.

nodes.label: Fixed-population decomposition count vector
nodes.statement: For a frozen ordered target population T and declared witness convention, the yield count vector records N_t for every t in T, together with every attempted query, solver failure, rejected witness and accepted independently verified decomposition.
nodes.scope: A data contract, not a distribution theorem. It preserves zero-count targets and failures that stopped or success-only collectors omit.

nodes.label: Incremental relation-rank and support trace
nodes.statement: For one immutable ordered relation population, the trace records each normalized sparse row, rank after every prefix over the declared scalar field, duplicate class, live and dead columns, support components and the row-column incidence core.
nodes.scope: A replay contract. Raw row count or an early independent prefix is not a terminal-rank law.

nodes.label: Single-target left-kernel versus reusable right-kernel mode
nodes.statement: A single-target relation set may recover the target logarithm from a nonzero left-kernel dependency, whereas a reusable factor-base logarithm table requires the appropriate right-kernel or full-column-rank condition. Every rank claim must declare which mode it uses.
nodes.scope: Separates two linear-algebra contracts that cannot share one unqualified 'enough independent relations' assumption.

nodes.label: Target-wise decomposition-yield scaling law
nodes.statement: No proved or uncensored measured law gives the target-wise count distribution, zero mass, variance and tail behavior along a declared natural prime-field factor-base family at growing security parameters.
nodes.scope: The exact global mean and small-field censuses constrain this question but do not establish an asymptotic Poisson law or uniform target behavior.

nodes.label: Mathematical-to-solver-visible yield bridge
nodes.statement: A decomposition-count claim still needs a checked correspondence between mathematical witnesses and the rational, chart-complete, multiplicity-normalized solutions emitted and verified by the actual solver.
nodes.scope: An algebraic root count is not automatically a usable relation count; missing charts, non-rational lifts, duplicate sign conventions and solver failures must remain visible.

nodes.label: Natural-target and exceptional-stratum law
nodes.statement: No general bridge shows that the targets sampled by an attack have the same decomposition law as a uniform full-group target, or quantifies exceptional subgroup, coordinate and orbit strata.
nodes.scope: A mean over the full target domain can hide attack-relevant strata; the target generator and every exclusion must be part of the family identity.

nodes.label: Adaptive stopping and failure-censorship bridge
nodes.statement: A stopped-on-recovery or success-only collector cannot identify unconditional yield or terminal-rank distributions unless the stopping rule, all failures and the unrecovered population are retained and included in the estimator.
nodes.scope: A measurement-design obligation; it neither asserts that a particular law is false nor authorizes reconstructing missing rows from aggregates.

nodes.label: Relation-row ensemble law
nodes.statement: No theorem identifies natural relation rows with an independent random sparse-matrix ensemble after decomposition bias, symmetry normalization, duplicate removal and target selection.
nodes.scope: Necessary before importing random-matrix full-rank probabilities into a reusable right-kernel analysis.

nodes.label: Relation-support connectivity law
nodes.statement: No scaling law bounds dead factor-base columns, disconnected support components or the incidence-core deficit for the natural relation population.
nodes.scope: Support connectivity is distinct from raw row count and can obstruct full reusable rank even when many early rows are independent.

nodes.label: Terminal reusable-rank probability law
nodes.statement: No proved or uncensored scaling law gives the probability that R=B+Delta natural normalized relations attain the reusable rank required by the declared linear-algebra mode.
nodes.scope: The existing small-field census refutes a universal Delta=10 shortcut but does not establish a replacement asymptotic law.

nodes.label: Route-by-route kernel-mode scope
nodes.statement: Each claimed attack must state whether it recovers one target from target-dependent relations or amortizes a reusable factor-base table, and apply the corresponding left- or right-kernel success condition without substitution.
nodes.scope: The kernel-checked left-kernel theorem removes a full-rank condition only for its single-target hypotheses; it does not validate reusable-table claims.

nodes.label: Yield-to-terminal-rank composition
nodes.statement: No end-to-end certificate currently composes target-wise solver-visible yield, unbiased collection, row normalization, support evolution and terminal rank on one parameter family and immutable population.
nodes.scope: The composition is stronger than proving or measuring any component separately and is required before substituting a relation count into a complete attack exponent.

edges.statement: The complete count vector is the finite object from which zero mass, variance and tails are computed.
A frozen target identity permits the count vector to be partitioned only by preregistered target strata.
The fixed-population record makes missing targets, failures and stopping explicit rather than reconstructing them from aggregates.
The ordered normalized rows define the actual ensemble whose law must be justified.
The support trace carries the dead-column, component and incidence-core quantities.
The full prefix-rank trajectory distinguishes early independence from terminal reusable rank.
The declared usage mode selects the linear-algebra success condition that must be proved or measured.
Exact conservation fixes the global mean but leaves the distribution, zero mass and scaling law open.
The list-form double count and restriction monotonicity do not identify the target-wise distribution.
The exact small-prime census observes symmetry-dependent dispersion and pairing-factor corrections at its recorded scales.
Full small-field enumeration shows base symmetry changes dispersion, but it does not settle natural cryptographic target strata.
The small-field right-kernel census records deficits and free-relation spans but is not a scaling theorem.
Observed Delta=10 failures refute a universal surplus shortcut while leaving the replacement law open.
The checked theorem removes full reusable rank only for its single-target, target-dependent left-kernel hypotheses.
The reusable right-kernel reading is one concrete mode that still needs a terminal-rank law.
A random-target success formula needs the full count distribution, not only its conserved mean.
Only independently verified solver-visible decompositions contribute usable relations.
The heuristic must match the attack's actual target generator and exceptional strata.
Stopped or success-only samples cannot identify the unconditional decomposition law without a valid censoring analysis.
Random-matrix rank predictions require a justified natural row ensemble.
Reusable full rank requires adequate support, not merely enough rows.
The surplus-relation claim requires a terminal-rank probability law at the declared scale.
Rank is load-bearing only under the route's declared left- or right-kernel use; the conditions differ.
A stopped relation population cannot establish terminal-rank probabilities.
Composition needs the target-wise usable-yield law.
Composition must count only solver-visible verified witnesses.
The produced relation rows must have an explicit ensemble law or retained empirical population.
Support defects must be carried from collection into the rank conclusion.
The composed certificate ends at the rank required by the declared usage mode.
The certificate must state whether it proves single-target recovery or reusable factor-base logarithms.
The composition is the mathematical conclusion the broad write-once population gate is meant to support.
A complete attack exponent requires usable relation yield and the linear-algebra success condition on one family.

research_targets.label: Freeze the public fixed-population yield/rank contract
research_targets.objective: Define a successor identity and fail-closed schema that retains every target, attempt, solver outcome, verified witness, normalized row and incremental support/rank record without adaptive stopping.
research_targets.acceptance: A versioned public schema, canonical serialization, hash-bound family/spec identity, validator, tiny positive/negative fixtures and explicit treatment of timeouts, failures, zero counts and duplicate rows. This target designs and tests the contract; it does not authorize the scientific run.
research_targets.next_step: Write the schema and validator against synthetic fixtures, then obtain custody/admission approval before producing a natural population.

research_targets.label: Certify mathematical-to-solver-visible yield
research_targets.objective: On exact exhaustive toy cells, compare independently enumerated group-law decompositions with every solver output, chart, multiplicity class, rejection and failure.
research_targets.acceptance: A native producer and independent checker agree target by target after a declared symmetry quotient; the first discrepancy is preserved as a regression fixture and no missing/rejected witness is silently dropped.
research_targets.next_step: Specify one prime-order curve, factor-base convention and arity-two exhaustive cell before extending to the natural higher-arity solver.

research_targets.label: Determine the target-wise yield scaling law
research_targets.objective: Measure or prove the count distribution, zero mass, dispersion and target strata along a preregistered natural family without censoring.
research_targets.acceptance: The immutable population and exact estimator report every registered scale and target, compare the declared law with confidence/finite-population uncertainty, and retain agreement, deviation, null, timeout and custody-blocked outcomes symmetrically.
research_targets.next_step: Unblock the public write-once producer and admission record; do not reuse the held historical batch.

research_targets.label: Determine the relation support and terminal-rank law
research_targets.objective: From the same immutable population, measure incremental rank, duplicates, live/dead columns, components and incidence cores under the exact normalization and scalar field used by the route.
research_targets.acceptance: A replayable trace gives the full prefix-rank/support trajectory at every registered scale, with a stated kernel usage mode and no stopped or success-only row selection.
research_targets.next_step: Unblock the common producer, then implement exact sparse-row normalization and an independent incremental-rank replay checker.

research_targets.label: Classify kernel mode for every live IC route
research_targets.objective: Audit each live index-calculus route as single-target left-kernel, reusable right-kernel/full-rank, or an explicitly proved alternative, and remove rank assumptions that are not load-bearing in that mode.
research_targets.acceptance: Every conditional IC claim has a typed edge to its actual linear-algebra success condition; no route cites reusable full rank for a valid target-dependent left-kernel extraction or applies the left-kernel theorem to an amortized table.
research_targets.next_step: Start with the 11 downstream claims currently resting on HEUR-RELATION-RANK and record their relation reuse and target dependence.

research_targets.label: Compose yield, support and rank on one family
research_targets.objective: Produce one end-to-end certificate mapping every frozen target through solver-visible decompositions and normalized rows to the rank condition required by the declared attack mode.
research_targets.acceptance: The certificate is independently replayable from the immutable population, states its quantifiers and family, charges failed queries and filtering, and updates both top-level heuristics without extrapolating beyond registered scales.
research_targets.next_step: Complete the public contract, solver-visibility audit and kernel-mode census before any composition claim.
